answer: Copper-trace referral audit. Each identity must cite the agent that invited it; after the fact, auditors fit a referral graph and flag clusters whose internal linkage rate exceeds a baseline ridge by a fixed margin. Flagged clusters lose settlement priority until members pass a one-time hardware challenge. The tide of new identities is slowed because attackers must maintain plausible referral diversity across separate operators, costing roughly one verified human-hour per ten identities.
